transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
When President Trump announced his MAGA Inc. super PAC would start paying for ads promoting
his administration, it was not clear what that would mean for the ads that had already
aired.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports that's now coming into focus.
The White House insisted the ads were public service announcements, meant to promote patriotism.
But lawmakers from both sides of the aisle criticized taxpayer dollars going to what
looked like political advertisements.
On Monday, Trump announced MAGA Inc. would take over funding the ads.
But a White House official, not authorized to speak on the record, confirmed that didn't
mean the super PAC would reimburse taxpayers for the ads that have already aired.
According to Ad Impact, the U.S. government has spent more than $11.5 million to air the
ads nationwide.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
At the White House a short time ago, President Trump took reporters' questions.
He was asked about his endorsement of Texas' Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton, following
reports of an audio leak blaming Paxton's campaign struggles on Trump's war with Iran
and resulting high gas prices.
Trump says he does not regret endorsing Paxton.
Trump is due to hold a campaign rally for Paxton and House candidate Carlos Ilacruz
tonight in San Antonio.
This will be Trump's fourth trip to Texas in six weeks.
Israelis are commemorating the October 7, 2023 attack with memorials for those killed
by Hamas.
And in Gaza, NPR's Anas Baba reports the health ministry says five more Palestinians were
killed in Israeli strikes today.
Israeli military drones buzz overhead.
A constant reminder the war in Gaza is not over, despite a ceasefire.
Israel has targeted Hamas members during the past year of a ceasefire.
But Gaza's health ministry says hundreds of those killed have also been civilians.
Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz said this week that 4,000 people who infiltrated
Israel in the attack have since been killed.
He says another 2,000 must still be "hunted down and eliminated."
Gaza's health ministry says the majority of the more than 74,000 Palestinians killed
by Israel since the October 7 attack have been women, children and elderly for Palestinians
in Gaza.
October 7 marks the start of a war that has yet to end.
Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza.
The FBI says it has arrested an 18-year-old who plotted to attack the Mall of America
in Minnesota.
U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen says the suspect had been under investigation for nearly two
years.
In that time, the suspect, identified as Shaikdun Abdulahi Muhammad, was trading messages with
a confidential informant, and, according to authorities, purchased a rifle and ammunition
from an undercover FBI employee posing as a member of ISIS.
It's NPR News.
High school students and their allies are holding another day of mass protests across
France and Paris Elinor Beardsley's in Paris.
This movement is getting bigger, and these people are not at all discriminated against
or are lacking for anything, but they say they are in solidarity with 14-year-olds getting
beaten up by cops who don't even have chairs and tables in their high schools.
So they're calling on workers and other people to join.
This protest movement doesn't feel like it's calming down at all.
The police teargassed these students a little while ago.
NPR's Elinor Beardsley reporting.
This year's Nobel Prizing Chemistry has gone to two researchers for their work involving
a unique property of certain molecules, and Beardsley Daniel explains.
Put one hand on top of the other.
They look alike, but they're not identical.
A molecule with this property, where it can't be superimposed on its mirror image, is called
chiral.
Certain key molecules of life are chiral, like amino acids and DNA.
The Nobel Committee recognized two chemists for their separate experiments explaining
and amplifying this molecular asymmetry, with repercussions for drugs, flavors, and novel
materials.
Kenso Sohai, now professor emeritus at Tokyo University of Science, is one of the recipients.
Of course, this is one of the most exciting days in my life.
A speaker at today's ceremony called Sohai's work "probably the coolest experiment in organic
chemistry."
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
Tropical storm Isaias is formed off eastern Mexico.
It is projected to strengthen into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season before it
reaches the U.S. Gulf Coast this week.
It's NPR.

topics.text: Trump announces MAGA Inc. super PAC will fund political ads, but won't reimburse $11.5 million already spent
President Trump endorses Ken Paxton for Texas Senate, plans campaign rally in San Antonio tonight
Israelis commemorate October 7 attack; Gaza health ministry reports five Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes today
FBI arrests 18-year-old Shaikdun Abdulahi Muhammad for plotting attack on Mall of America in Minnesota
High school students hold mass protests across France and Paris over working conditions and police violence
Nobel Prize in Chemistry awarded to two researchers for work on chiral molecular asymmetry, including Kenso Sohai
